title: Context Fabric Bounded Context document, contract 1
description: The context one set of workflows needs: which organizations it draws on, which of their systems it actually uses, where those systems were reached from, and what it could not reach. It references Org facts rather than copying them, so an Org document's next release is the only place that fact changes.
$comment: This directory is released and immutable. A change of shape creates schemas/bounded-context/2/ with a migration step beside it.

allOf.$comment: The tier is shared, so the reasoning that keeps secrets and machine paths out of an Org document is identical here.

id.description: This document's identifier, stable across every move and rename.

kind.description: Which contract this document is written against.

schema_version.description: The contract version this document is written against.

identity.description: What this context is and who it is for.

organizations.description: The organizations this context draws on. A team whose work crosses an organizational boundary is the ordinary case, not an exception.

extends.description: The documents this context reads facts from, each with the release it was written against and where to read it.

source_selection.description: Which source of a fact this context uses and why the others were not chosen. The rejected entries are the valuable ones: without them the same argument is had again every quarter.

repositories.description: The repositories this context's workflows touch.

systems.description: The systems this context uses, each either referenced in the Org document that owns it or declared here when no document owns it yet.

anchors.description: Concrete places a workflow starts: a saved query, a dashboard, a folder. An anchor is what turns 'we use that system' into something a newcomer can open.

outputs.description: Who the generated views are for and where they land.

limitations.description: What this context does not cover, in the reader's terms. An empty list is a claim that somebody looked.

access_failures.description: What this context tried to reach and could not. Recorded rather than dropped: an absence with no reason reads as a system nobody needed.

identity.title: Identity
identity.description: What this context is, said once, so every generated view can open with it.

name.description: What the team calls this context.

purpose.description: What somebody can do with this context that they could not do without it.

audience.description: Who the context is written for, when that is narrower than everyone who can read it.

source_choice.title: Source choice
source_choice.description: One decision about where a fact comes from.

id.description: The identifier of the fact or feed the choice is about.

source.description: The source itself, named the way the team names it.

status.description: Whether this source is the one to use, the one to fall back to, or one that was considered and rejected.

rationale.description: Why. A rejected source with no reason gets proposed again next quarter.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: A repository this context's workflows touch.

id.description: The repository's identifier within this context.

purpose.description: What this context uses it for.

coverage.description: How much of the repository this context works in: the whole of it, or part. An agent deciding whether a file is in scope branches on this, so it is a value rather than a sentence.

path_scope.description: The paths within the repository this context works in, relative to its root. Required when coverage is partial. An entry names a place INSIDE the repository, so it never starts with / and never climbs out with a .. segment.

system_use.title: System use
system_use.description: One system this context uses, and how far anybody here has actually got with it.

ref.description: The system in the Org document that owns it, as <document-id>#<system-id>.

declared.description: A system no published document owns yet. A stopgap, and the rationale is what keeps it from becoming permanent.

scope.description: Whether somebody here has actually used this system. `established` is a claim that a person reached it and can point at where they started.

anchors.description: The anchors in this document that name where work on this system starts.

limitations.description: What this context cannot do with this system, beyond whatever the owning document already says.

allOf.$comment: Either referenced or declared, never both and never neither: a system with two descriptions has no owner.
An established system without an anchor is a claim nobody can check.

declared_system.title: Declared system
declared_system.description: A system this context depends on that no Org document publishes yet.

id.description: The system's identifier within this document.

kind.description: What kind of thing it is.

status.description: Where it sits in its life.

rationale.description: Why it is declared here instead of referenced, which is also the note that makes moving it somebody's job.

anchor.title: Anchor
anchor.description: A concrete place a workflow starts.

id.description: The anchor's identifier within this document.

label.description: What a reader will see when they open it.

note.description: What somebody needs to know before opening it.

outputs.title: Outputs
outputs.description: Who the generated views serve and where they are written.

roles.description: The roles the views are written for.

guidance.description: What a reader should do with the view, in one sentence.

destination.description: Where the generated views are written.

access_failure.title: Access failure
access_failure.description: Something this context tried to reach and could not.

system.description: What was being reached, named however the team names it.

outcome.description: What happened, and what would have to change.

allOf.$comment: Relative to the repository root. A leading slash reads as a path on somebody machine.
No .. segment anywhere, for the same reason a location may not have one: a rule about net escape asks every reviewer to redo the arithmetic.

path_scope_entry.title: Path scope entry
path_scope_entry.description: One path inside a repository, relative to its root. Names a place in the repository, so it never starts with / and never climbs out with a .. segment.
